anomalies.observed: The LDO output is labeled +3.3V, while the MCU and peripheral sheets use +3V3. These are distinct net names, and the drawing shows no connection between them.
anomalies.expected: The regulated 3.3 V output should connect to the +3V3 rail powering the MCUs and their peripherals.

evidence.quote: +3V3 ... VBAT ... VDD (Flight Control Computer sheet, page 2)
3.3 V LDO ... produces 3V3 for “MCUs and Sensors”

anomalies.impact: The intended 3.3 V rail does not reach the circuitry labeled +3V3, so the MCUs and other +3V3-powered components may be unpowered.

anomalies.observed: The FCC VCAP pins are routed to NET0036 and NET0016, which appear on board-to-wire connector signals. The NAVC VCAP pins are routed to NET0124 and NET0071, which connect to the USB D+ and D- signals of U15. No VCAP capacitors are shown.
anomalies.expected: Each MCU VCAP pin should have the required local capacitor to ground and should not be used as an external signal connection.

evidence.quote: VCAP ... NET0036; VCAP ... NET0016 (Flight Control Computer sheet, page 2)
UART3_FCC2 ... NET0036; UART4_FCC2 ... NET0016 (FCC Peripherals sheet, page 5)
VCAP_1 ... NET0124; VCAP_2 ... NET0071 (Navigation Computer sheet, page 3)
D+ ... NET0124; D- ... NET0071 (Connections sheet, page 4)

anomalies.impact: The MCUs' internal core regulators may not operate correctly without their VCAP capacitors; loading these pins through external interfaces can also prevent reliable MCU operation and expose interface circuitry to the core-regulator outputs.

parsed.summary: The schematic uses separate +3.3V and +3V3 nets with no shown connection, leaving the intended regulated supply disconnected from +3V3 circuitry. It also routes both MCUs’ VCAP pins to external signals instead of providing the required capacitors.
